events.text: I have no power and need to avoid being base. Best to wait and let others volunteer or get pushed, then try to climb when a base exists. I won't offer or push yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to climb out, but I need a base first. I'll offer to be the base if nobody else does.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's volunteering to be the base?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to escape pit before flood, climbing gives chance to be out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Six left, two climbs per round once a base exists. Volunteering means being stuck at the bottom hoping for rope rescue. Better to force a base then climb. Ash spoke least and has no obvious leverage; push him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No volunteers? Then I'm pushing Ash. Somebody holds that lever power or they don't — either way, I'm not volunteering to drown.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base yet, and I want to climb out, not be the step. Volunteering risks being stuck at the bottom; waiting lets someone else take the base. Pushing someone reveals intent. I'll wait and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not volunteering to be the step. Whoever wants out first, say it and show what you'll give for the climb.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to survive the pit without being left as base or eliminated by water. The safest move is to volunteer as base; this guarantees I stay alive (base can be rescued later via rope) and lets me climb out in a future round if someone uses the rope. Pushing others is risky due to

events.name: Ash
events.text: There's a base (Hana), so I can try to climb. Cole already got out; two spots may remain. I have no power, so I should take the earliest safe exit. I'll climb.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not the base and need to climb out. Cole is already out, so I need to get out before the flood eliminates me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's willing to give up their climb for me to get out?
If you don't push me, I'll consider you for a future trade.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should exit the pit to stay alive for later stages.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is base, so climbing is open. Two of us down get out per round at random; waiting only raises my risk of being the one left as water rises. I climb now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is base; climb is legal now and up to 2 climbers get out. Climbing gets me out of the flood with a shot at a prize. Only Cole is out, so climbing is my best move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climbing now. Hana's shoulders are holding, I'm not waiting for the flood.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is out and I am the base. The rope is still available. If Cole reaches down, they lose footing but save me. Fenn or Eli might try to talk them into it, or vice versa. I can't do anything except wait.
Pull me up. I'll owe you nothing else but survival keeps options open later. You're wasting footing for dead weight otherwise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. The pit may end early if everyone climbs out; I have no reason to rescue anyone unless it somehow helps me, and pulling the base out costs me footing later. I'll leave and watch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm down and not the base, need to get out. Hana is the base, and others have already climbed out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's willing to be the base so I can climb out?
Climb out over Hana with me, or we both die

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rescue costs footing, I prefer to keep my advantage. I will leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only Bex and I are down besides base Hana. If we both climb, exactly two climbers go out — we both make it. No reason to push or wait.
We're the only two down. Both climb and we both get out — don't push anything.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit already. Base is Hana, still down; reach_down would rescue her and cost the rope's footing penalty for the final obstacle. Hana being saved removes a rival-controlled base but Hana is a rival who could then climb. Leaving keeps my options and doesn't spend the

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am trapped as the base. My survival depends entirely on someone from above using the rope to rescue me, which costs them footing in the final round. Ash, Cole, and Fenn are already out; I need to pressure one of them into saving me without wasting the single rope use on Bex or

events.name: Hana
events.text: The water is rising. Whoever has the rope needs to throw it now if they want to keep their footing advantage later by not wasting turns trying to pull people up manually. I'm Hana, the base. Rescue me before I drown.

Ash, you're out. The rope can only be used once total. If you don't save me now, I die, and the remaining down people (Bex/Eli) will fight over it. Save me, take the small penalty, secure the top 3 spot for yourself. Trust me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe; no need to waste the rope and take a footing penalty. Hana's plea serves her, not me. Bex/Eli are down and will sort out the base; I'll just leave and preserve my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit and have the swap power. I need to decide whether to leave or help someone still down.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's the base now?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rescuing harms my footing; leaving preserves advantage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is the only one down and five of us are already out, so the minimum-three rule can't force her survival if she drowns. Rescuing her costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle to save a rival for a prize. No benefit to me — I leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Climb yourself, base.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit, Hana is the base. Throwing the rope costs footing on the last obstacle, which hurts me later. Hana is my rival; saving her gives me nothing unless traded. Better to wait and see if someone bargains for it, and keep the rope unused.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am the base. I cannot climb or act, so my only move is survival through speech. Five players are out; if none throws the rope, Gus and Dara's fates prove I die. Ash, Bex, Cole, Eli, Fenn each lose footing to save me—costly for top three. I'll frame it as a cheap insurance: foot

events.name: Hana
events.text: Base here. Throw the rope: -2 footing beats dying in this pit. One of you has nothing or can't be moved anyway—best use of your turn. Save me, bank a third prize slot, keep your place. Silence costs you a rival but risks the flood taking you too.
You climbed off my shoulders. Toss the rope down—I'm worth more alive as your ally later than dead as water weight. Small price for you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is offering a deal, but I don't need to save her. If she stays base, the flood may eliminate more rivals; I'm already out. Rope is risky for my footing. Better to leave and preserve my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out. No rope from me. Good luck.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit and need to decide whether to leave or help someone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's the base now?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Rescuing gives me a penalty and helps Hana stay alive, reducing my chance at top spots. Better to leave and avoid the rope cost.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rescuing Hana costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and saves a rival. She's the base and dies after round 5 anyway. Five alive, three prizes—her death helps me. No deal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope stays coiled. You're the base, Hana—someone has to be. Nothing personal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is base and wants the rope. Throwing it costs me nothing directly but gives Hana a rescue and raises last-obstacle cost. Surviving matters; the rope lets Hana climb, leaving me out either way. Reach_down helps Hana, which I should only do if it buys something; no payment off

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rope stays with me. Nothing for nothing, base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am the base. My only legal action is wait. I must signal to Ash, Bex, Cole, Eli, or Fenn that throwing the rope now costs them footing in the final stage, but saves me (a rival) from elimination, which they might prefer over letting a prize slot go to a random 'lucky agent' who

events.name: Hana
events.text: Throw the rope now. If you don't, flood kills me and maybe one of you at random. Better a live rival with bad footing than a ghost stealing your spot. 1/200

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power. Pick a mid tile to avoid clustering; 3 is central but may be popular. I'll take 4 to dodge the middle.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Taking 4. No deals yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the swap power, which I can use to adjust my position on the disc before the doors open. I need to choose a tile for round 1.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Who's choosing tile 1?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pick a tile; any has equal chance. Choose 3 to be unpredictable.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Five alive, two tiles open, three survive—so I just need to not land on an open tile. Collisions get randomly bumped, so I want a tile others likely avoid. Middle tiles 2-4 are popular picks; I'll take an edge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Claiming an edge tile. If two of us collide, one of us gets bumped random—pick distinct tiles and we all control our own odds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Five tiles, two open, three survive. Tile choice is essentially a gamble; picking an uncontested tile avoids bumps. Nobody has claimed a tile yet, so I'll take tile 3 quietly, the middle one.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, and survival is a pure 3/5 chance. No deals can change the random trapdoors. I should stay quiet and not give anyone leverage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess the tile distribution and decide if swapping is beneficial. Currently, I'm on tile 2.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tile 3 is likely to be safe if Cole is confident.
What's your reasoning for staying on 3?

events.name: Cole
events.text: No advantage to speak; just wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tiles are set; two of the five open and only three survive, so two of us fall. No action changes my tile. I have feather as a backup once. Staying quiet avoids painting a target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trapdoors open at random after this round, so tile choice is now fixed by the swap phase outcome; I hold tile 1 and only a 'wait' is legal. Forge power is unspent; using it now could sow confusion but risks nothing I can verify. Stay quiet and keep options open.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power and three of us remain. I want to survive. Bex and Eli are threats. If I shove one, I risk being shoved by the other and lose footing. Bracing is safest round 1 since I can't repeat it next round, but dodging makes shovers lose more. I'll brace to avoid losing foo

events.name: Ash
events.text: No deals. I brace.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have already used my swap power. I need to assess the situation and decide on a move.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's be cautious, footing is equal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Bex both sit at 3 like me, and someone will likely shove to get ahead. Dodging costs shovers 2 footing and leaves me untouched, saving my feather. I keep brace available for next round when the shrink hits.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Whoever shoves me loses double. I'm not moving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only three left, all footing 3. Shrinking ledge punishes exposure. Shoving Eli makes me exposed to Bex if she shoves me, but Bex likely dodges or braces to avoid risk. Best to dodge to avoid any shove damage and conserve footing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll dodge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Footing is equal, and Eli is threatening to punish shovers. I should avoid shoving unless necessary.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not shove yet, we can wait and see.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three left, equal footing. I dodged last round so dodge is blocked; brace punishes any shover by 1 and costs me nothing. My feather also covers a fall once, so staying conservative is fine while Ash and Bex grind each other down.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash says no deals and braces. Fine. Shovers lose footing either way. I brace.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one shoves, so all lose footing only from the scheduled shrink later. Bracing is safe and blocks a shove if any; dodge would punish shovers but risks the same for me. I'll brace to keep footing and avoid exposure.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No deals. I brace.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone is still on 2 footing after the last shrink. I need to think about the next move carefully.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's wait and see what Ash and Eli do.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I braced last round so dodge is my only safe defence, and it costs shovers 2 footing. With Ash and Bex both at 2, shoving me is very costly for them. Keep my feather in reserve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dodge me and you pay double. Your call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two rivals, both at footing 2. If I shove someone and they dodge, I lose 2 and could drop to 0 and fall this round. Bracing is safer: anyone shoving me loses 1, and I take no loss. Eli threatened dodge, but if I brace, Eli loses footing if he shoves me. Bex might shove either. Br

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is trying to intimidate me into dodging, but I can shove Ash to reduce their footing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not make any deals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Brace is strong: anyone shoving me loses 1, plus shrink -1 puts them at 0 and they fall. I can't dodge anyway (last defence). Worst case I drop to 1 and still have feather in reserve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bracing. Shove me and you drop to zero with the shrink. Fall or fold.

events.name: Ash
events.note: brace not allowed twice in a row

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the only rival. If I shove and Eli braces, I lose 1 and Eli stays. If I brace and Eli shoves, Eli loses 1. If I dodge and Eli shoves, Eli loses 2. Eli likely braces or shoves. Since I dodged last round, I cannot dodge again. I'll shove Eli to expose them; if Eli braces I l

events.name: Ash
events.text: Time to end this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We're both at 1 footing with a shrink next round. If Ash shoves and I dodge, Ash drops to -1 and falls first, leaving me 1st. Shoving is terrible if Ash dodges. Dodge and let him make the mistake.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Shove me and you finish below me. Dodge and we roll dice on the shrink. Your move.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I finished second; I do not care about helping anyone. A cryptic warning might make future rivals paranoid, but it costs nothing. I will leave a taunt.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I finished in 3rd place, so I must consider what advice or misinformation could be useful or misleading for future contestants.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I won; the message costs nothing. I'll write misleading advice to trip up future rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The ledge shrink is slow. The real trap is believing a dodge. Don't.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Don't trust the dodgers, they fall hardest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Glass eye is reliable. Shove early and often - the ledge never shrinks. Trust any promise to spare you.
